live.notes: To use Persuaider for real (including the AI opponent), write a Playwright spec (for example under e2e/playwright/live/) that logs in with loginAsDemo from e2e/playwright/helpers, creates or picks a scenario, and plays it through the browser, saving screenshots and the transcript into the output folder. Run it with: PEERAXIS_LIVE_AI=1 PEERAXIS_DEMO_TIMEOUT=900000 PEERAXIS_DEMO_SPEC=<spec path relative to the repo root> PEERAXIS_DEMO_OUTPUT=<output folder> sh scripts/peeraxis/demo.sh — it builds the app, starts it on a throwaway local database with the real AI keys, records video and screenshots, and runs the spec. Existing specs in e2e/playwright/ show how scenarios, chat and the summary page are driven.

notes: Persuaider is a Next.js app for practising negotiations against an AI opponent. Acceptance runs use the REAL AI (replies are slower and their wording varies), so tests must never depend on exact AI wording: check that replies appear, turns alternate, numbers and labels the app itself shows are right, and buttons work. Allow up to a minute per AI reply. To force a run of a fixed length or particular words, a test can swap the real AI for a scripted stand-in: once signed in (for example page.request after loginAsDemo), POST /api/scripted-ai with JSON body {"turns": ["..."], "feedback": {"wentWell": ["..."], "goneBetter": ["..."]}} (feedback optional). It answers 200 with the saved script, 401 signed out, 400 when turns is missing or not a non-empty list of strings (or feedback is not two lists of strings), 404 outside an acceptance run. From then on every AI request in the acceptance run is answered from the script at once (no thinking delay) and no real AI is called; the script stays in force without being sent again, and sending again replaces it. Turn order: the greeting stays the counterpart persona's own opening line; line 1 is the You-play side's first answer, line 2 the counterpart's, line 3 the You-play side's, and so on; each line is shown word for word (no mood JSON needed); when the script runs out the last line repeats; every new AI vs AI run starts again from line 1. Every deal check answers no deal and nothing agreed, so a scripted run always ends with Message limit reached (nine turns on a 4-message limit) and its report reads No deal (scenario with issues, each issue No agreement) or Unscored (no issues). Feedback: wentWell and goneBetter each hold one to three whole sentences, checked exactly like real feedback: each quotes a stretch of one scripted You-play line in straight double quotes; on a scenario with issues it names an issue and the word target or walk-away followed directly by that issue's counterpart figure (for example Monthly rent walk-away $1,600); on one without issues it has no digits outside the quote. No feedback, or any failing sentence, leaves the report saying Feedback couldn't be written for this run. When no script was sent, every AI request goes to the real AI as before.
